title: How can the plus figure keep only two angles of symmetry?
description: The plus-shaped figure with four radial arms is changed so that a quarter turn no longer fits but a half turn still does. The top arm bends right at its end, the bottom arm bends left, and the side arms stay straight. Keeko's doubt is that bending all four arms the same way leaves only two angles.
teaching_notes: One idea: a quarter turn must fail and a half turn must still fit, so opposite arms are alike and neighbouring arms differ. Watch for students who bend every arm the same way and still get four angles.

source: How will you modify the plus-shaped figure with 4 radial arm
video_script.why: The child changes the four-arm figure so that only the half turn and the full turn fit.
video_script.substitution: the book's plus figure, with the top arm bent right at its end and the bottom arm bent left
video_script.anchor: the book's plus-shaped figure with four radial arms and a dot at its centre
video_script.wrong_answer: bend all four arms the same way
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko bends every arm to the right and thinks only two angles are left.
video_script.payoff_line: Only the half turn and the full turn fit

final_answer.value: Bend the top arm right and the bottom arm left; only 180° and 360° fit
final_answer.spoken: bend the top arm to the right and the bottom arm to the left; only one hundred eighty and three hundred sixty degrees fit

maths_rules: the plus figure has 4 angles of symmetry: 90°, 180°, 270°, 360°
to keep only 2 angles of symmetry, a quarter turn (90°) must not fit and the half turn (180°) must fit
top arm bent right at its end, bottom arm bent left (its half turn copy), left and right arms straight
quarter turn: the bent top arm lands on a straight side arm, no fit
half turn: top arm lands on bottom arm and left arm lands on right arm, fit
so the angles of symmetry are 180° and 360°
video_script.design: The plus figure is drawn with a bend at the end of the top and bottom arms. A quarter turn is tried and fails, then a half turn is tried and fits. Keeko's doubt is that bending all four arms the same way is enough.
